title: Charles Whitworth to Secretary Boyle, Moscow, September and October 1708 (TNA SP 91/5): a partial table of the envoy's numerical code rebuilt from the office's decipherment written above the groups, and tested once on a bare duplicate

plaintext.source: No decipherment on this copy. The despatch is printed, from the copy the office deciphered, in Sbornik vol. 50 (1886) No. 22, pp. 44-49 (an extract that contains all the coded passages). The original in the same volume (stamped f. 42) is catalogued 'partly in cipher' and presumably carries the office's words; not seen.

transcription.source: State Papers Online, 1509-1714 (Gale) page images, seen under a library licence; not reproduced
transcription.notes: Held-out letter of the key test. All six pages read twice by two AI readers who saw only the images; the two give the same 112 code groups in the same places (five carry a second reading in one pass). A third AI reader checked about 54 of the groups on the images and read none differently. No person has checked it. 'not read' here is the key's result alone (47 of 77 coded words whole); the text itself has been in print since 1886.

system.summary: A numerical code of words, syllables and single letters, written as numbers separated by dots among clear words; numbers seen from 31 to 1503. The rebuilt part shows alphabetical runs: letters 31 (a) to 141 (y) with several numbers to a letter, syllables 146 (af) to 253 (wo), syllables and short words 264 (an) to 481 (well), then words (494 arm ... 597 writ; 601 your ... 713 was; and higher), with names and titles high in the range (1415 Archangel, 1423 Czar). Common words have more than one number (the 357, 469; and 496, 607).
system.notes: distinct_symbols = different numbers in the three letters together (the two originals of 22 Sept / 3 Oct and the duplicate of 1/12 Sept), one or two of them probably misreadings. 246 have a value in key.tsv. unread_groups = the 33 different numbers of the held-out duplicate that are not in the key. Phrases are single numbers (499 'by the', 674 'of the', 1047 'to the').

prior_solution.where: Deciphered in the Secretary of State's office in 1708: the words stand above the code groups on the received originals (SP 91/5, stamped ff. 90 and 110). Printed in English, from the deciphered copies, in Sbornik Imperatorskago Russkago Istoricheskago Obshchestva vol. 50 (St Petersburg 1886): No. 22 (1/12 Sept 1708), No. 27 and No. 28 (22 Sept / 3 Oct 1708). Recorded for lead 1151 in Andrew Beling's vetting of 14 Nov 2026. No table of the code was found in print or in this repository; the British Library's Whitworth papers (Add MS 37354-60) and Hartley's life of Whitworth (2002) were not searched.

conditions.human_role: Andrew Beling chose the lead, vetted it (14 Nov 2026), set the rules (two blind transcriptions; each test written with its pass mark and controls before it is run, and run once; a miss or a void reported as such) and gave the go-ahead for each test. AI agents located the sources, transcribed, built the table, ran the tests, checked and wrote. No person has read the numbers or the words against the images.
tools: frozen/scripts/wlib.py, wlib2.py, run_test2.py (alignment, table rule, held-out score, shuffled controls; Python standard library)
frozen/scripts/merge_passes.py, build_runs2.py (merging two blind transcriptions; pairing coded stretches with the print)
decode.py (this folder): applies key.tsv to the coded stretches and checks the decryption file

solution.what: Andrew Beling contribution: vetting of lead 1151. Sbornik vol. 50 (1886) found to print Whitworth's despatches from 24 March 1708 in English from deciphered copies; the 1708 items marked as already in print.

Andrew Beling contribution: the two bare duplicates of 22 Sept / 3 Oct 1708 (stamped ff. 112 and 114) read twice blind by AI readers: 357 and 473 groups, 352 and 468 agreed; ten disagreements looked at on enlarged crops, six left open. Sbornik Nos. 27 and 28 typed from the page images.

Andrew Beling contribution: first held-out test, plan and pass mark hashed beforehand. Table built by alignment from one duplicate (f. 114) and the 1886 print alone: 49 numbers. On the other duplicate (f. 112) 87 of 357 groups covered, 84 fit the print (0.966; shuffled tables 0.30 at the 99th percentile). The plan required 100 covered groups: VOID by its own rule. Table dropped.

Andrew Beling contribution: the deciphered originals found on State Papers Online at stamped ff. 110 and 90 (the catalogue's old ff. 294 and 274), with the office's words above the groups; typed once each. The 1886 print compared with them: the same text in the coded passages apart from spelling and five one-word differences in No. 27. A third bare duplicate found: stamped f. 49, the despatch of 1/12 Sept 1708.

Andrew Beling contribution: the duplicate of 1/12 Sept 1708 (stamped f. 49) read twice blind by two AI readers: 112 code groups each, identical in all 112. Sbornik No. 22 typed. The 15 coded stretches paired with the print by their clear-word neighbours (five boundaries set by hand from clear words and print alone).

Andrew Beling contribution: table of 246 numbers from the office's words above the groups on the two originals: 139 numbers standing alone under one word (tier S), 62 and 45 by a seeded alignment kept only where ten runs agree (tiers A, B). Rule chosen on the building letters only; table frozen by SHA-256 before the held-out file was opened.

Andrew Beling contribution: second held-out test, run once. On the duplicate of 1/12 Sept 1708: 78 of 112 groups in the table, 69 fit the 1886 print (0.885; pass mark 0.80); 1,000 shuffled tables: 99th percentile 0.17, highest 0.22. PASS, on a small sample. Nine misses: four the print's spelling, one word order, four the table's or the reading's (236 'post' is wrong, should be 'st').

Andrew Beling contribution: an AI agent that had not made the test checked the 17 hashes, reran the test from the frozen files (same table byte for byte, same scores), looked for a path from the held-out letter into the table (none found), and read 54 groups of f. 49 and 14 table values on the images. It found 236 wrong (st, not post) and 219 and 505 supported on the originals.

Andrew Beling contribution: the coded passages of the duplicate of 1/12 Sept written out with the key alone and counted by the strict rule: 47 of 77 coded words whole (0.61, an estimate). Marked 'decoded, not read'; the full text is the 1886 print's.

outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: The key was taken from the decipherment the Secretary of State's office wrote above the code groups on the received originals of 22 Sept / 3 Oct 1708 (SP 91/5, stamped ff. 90 and 110), and tested once on a bare duplicate of another despatch (stamped f. 49, 1/12 Sept 1708) against the text printed in 1886. The content is the office's and the print's; the table is the contribution.
outcome.fraction_read_source: reading_1708-09-01.md: coded words of the held-out duplicate of 1/12 Sept 1708 that the key gives whole, 47 of 77 (strict count: a word with any group missing or any letter supplied is a hole). An estimate, because the groups do not map to words one to one and the word list is the 1886 print's. The two letters of 22 Sept / 3 Oct are not in this figure: their text is the office's own.

validation.notes: Contributor's pre-registered held-out test (not docs/_validate.py), by AI agents. Plan and every input hashed before the run (frozen/plans/HASHES_2.txt); table frozen before the held-out file was opened; one measurement: 69 of 78 covered groups fit the 1886 print (0.885) against 0.17 for the 99th percentile of 1,000 shuffled tables; marks fixed in advance (at least 40 covered groups, H >= 0.80, margin >= 0.30). A small sample: 112 held-out groups, 78 covered. A first test on 21 Nov 2026 (table from the print alone) was void by its own rule, 87 covered groups where 100 were required (frozen/test1_void/). That the plans predate the runs rests on local hashes and clock times only. Key not changed after the measurement, although one value is now known to be wrong (236).

texts.label: The two received originals of 22 Sept / 3 Oct 1708 (SP 91/5, stamped ff. 90 and 110): code groups with the office's words above them
texts.summary: The material the key was built from: Whitworth's relation and private letter on the affront to the Russian ambassador Matveev in London, the Czar's resentment, the reparation demanded, the tobacco contract and the young Russian noblemen sailing from Archangel, with the decipherment of the Secretary of State's office written above the code groups.
texts.note: Line-by-line transcriptions of clear words, code groups and, in square brackets, the office's words above the groups (placed by eye, sometimes a group or two out). The decipherment is the office's of 1708, not a decryption made here; the same text is printed in Sbornik vol. 50 Nos. 27 and 28 (print/).

texts.label: Whitworth to Boyle, Moscow, 1/12 Sept 1708, bare duplicate (SP 91/5, stamped f. 49): the held-out letter
texts.summary: In the coded passages Whitworth says he has warned the English merchants not to engage too far on credit, since if the King of Sweden breaks in he cannot see where the Russians would raise money; their persons and effects will be safe at Archangel; the end of the war may be best observed by the ministers who follow that king; and on the affront to the ambassador he hopes to stop all by recrimination without seeming too much concerned (from the 1886 print; with the key alone 47 of the 77 coded words come out whole).
texts.note: decryption_1708-09-01.txt is key.tsv applied group by group, unedited, with the 1886 print's words for each stretch beside it and labelled as the print's. The reading marks every word the key does not give whole as a hole filled from the print.

outcome.notes: The despatches were deciphered at the time and printed in 1886, so no reading is claimed. What is new is part of the code as a reusable table (246 numbers), with a held-out test that passed on a small sample and an earlier one that was void. No image is reproduced: the page images are State Papers Online's (Gale), licensed.
